name: manual_eb056e
claim: When fixing automated-review findings (CodeRabbit, etc.) across a multi-language port of the same logic (e.g. a Python core + TypeScript core implementing one contract), always check whether the SAME bug class exists in the sibling language/test file too, even if the review only flagged one side -- automated reviewers commonly miss the parallel copy.

decisions.notes: On orama-system PR #338, CodeRabbit flagged a test-fixture bug in conformance.test.ts (makeEnv() silently enabling extra methods with no registered executor, producing unexpected attempt-log entries). The Python suite's test_conformance.py had the IDENTICAL bug in its equivalent test, never flagged by the review, confirmed red via an actual pytest run before fixing. Caught only because I habitually re-ran the full suite after applying review fixes rather than trusting the diff was complete.
